```{r setup}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(jsonlite)
  library(knitr)
})

if (!file.exists(params$report_data_path)) {
  stop("Report data file not found: ", params$report_data_path)
}
report <- readRDS(params$report_data_path)
fmt_int <- function(x) format(as.integer(x), big.mark = ",")
fmt_pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f %%", x)
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**Generated:** `r report$timestamp`
**Quality gate:** `r if (isTRUE(report$passed)) "**PASSED**" else "**FAILED**"`
**Total rows (unique EINs):** `r fmt_int(report$total_rows)`
**Source files stacked:** `r report$n_input_files`
**Vintages contributing rows:** `r report$n_vintages`
:::

# Summary

The Unified BMF is a single-row-per-EIN consolidation drawn from the
most-recent vintage in which each EIN appears across both the
current monthly BMF pipeline and the legacy 501CX-NONPROFIT-PX
pipeline. See [chapter 11](https://urbaninstitute.github.io/nccs-data-bmf/11-master-bmf.html)
for the full design.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total rows | `r fmt_int(report$total_rows)` |
| Distinct EINs | `r fmt_int(report$distinct_eins)` |
| Rows == distinct EINs (uniqueness gate) | `r if (isTRUE(report$ein_unique)) "✅ yes" else "❌ NO"` |
| Input CSV files | `r report$n_input_files` |
| Vintages with at least one surviving row | `r report$n_vintages` |

# Rows by source pipeline

```{r}
if (!is.null(report$rows_by_source) && length(report$rows_by_source$bmf_source) > 0) {
  src_dt <- data.table(
    bmf_source = report$rows_by_source$bmf_source,
    n_rows     = report$rows_by_source$n_rows
  )
  src_dt[, pct := round(100 * n_rows / sum(n_rows), 2)]
  kable(src_dt, format = "html",
        col.names = c("Source", "Rows", "Percent"),
        format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
}
```

# First / last year coverage

```{r}
yr <- report$year_range
yr_dt <- data.table(
  metric = c("Earliest first_year_in_bmf",
             "Latest first_year_in_bmf",
             "Earliest last_year_in_bmf",
             "Latest last_year_in_bmf"),
  value  = c(yr$min_first_year, yr$max_first_year,
             yr$min_last_year,  yr$max_last_year)
)
kable(yr_dt, format = "html",
      col.names = c("Metric", "Year"))
```

# Vintages observed per EIN

How many distinct BMF vintages did each EIN appear in?

```{r}
vo <- report$vintages_observed
vo_dt <- data.table(
  metric = c("Minimum",
             "Average",
             "Maximum",
             "EINs that appear in only one vintage"),
  value  = c(fmt_int(vo$min_vintages),
             sprintf("%.1f", as.numeric(vo$avg_vintages)),
             fmt_int(vo$max_vintages),
             fmt_int(vo$n_only_once))
)
kable(vo_dt, format = "html",
      col.names = c("Metric", "Value"))
```

# Vintage histogram

Number of surviving Unified BMF rows contributed by each vintage. A
vintage with many rows contributed many EINs whose latest sighting
was in that month.

```{r}
hist_df <- report$vintage_histogram
if (!is.null(hist_df) && nrow(hist_df) > 0) {
  hist_dt <- as.data.table(hist_df)
  setorder(hist_dt, -n_rows)
  kable(hist_dt, format = "html",
        col.names = c("Vintage (YYYY-MM)", "Source", "Rows contributed"),
        format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
}
```

# Column completeness

Top 30 most-complete columns (highest non-null fraction):

```{r}
# The completeness table carries an overall non-null share plus one share per
# source (current-monthly vs legacy rows). Label every column it has; a
# mismatch between the table and col.names aborts kable() and with it the
# whole render (that is what silently stopped the HTML on 2026-09-15).
comp <- as.data.table(report$completeness)
comp_cols <- intersect(c("column", "pct_non_null", "pct_current", "pct_legacy"),
                       names(comp))
comp <- comp[, ..comp_cols]
comp_names <- c(column = "Column", pct_non_null = "Non-null %",
                pct_current = "Current rows %", pct_legacy = "Legacy rows %")[comp_cols]
setorder(comp, -pct_non_null)
kable(head(comp, 30), format = "html", col.names = unname(comp_names))
```

Bottom 30 least-complete columns:

```{r}
setorder(comp, pct_non_null)
kable(head(comp, 30), format = "html", col.names = unname(comp_names))
```

# Columns populated by only one source

Columns that are well populated in one pipeline's rows and empty in the
other's. These are expected where a field exists in only one source (for
example fields the legacy extracts never carried), and worth a look where
it does not.

```{r}
flags <- report$source_completeness_flags
if (!is.null(flags) && nrow(flags) > 0) {
  flags <- as.data.table(flags)[, ..comp_cols]
  kable(flags, format = "html", col.names = unname(comp_names))
} else {
  cat("None.")
}
```

# Derived organization columns

NCCS works out three columns from the IRS codes of each organization:
its role (`nccs_org_role`), its legal type (`nccs_org_legal_type`) and
the field it works in (`nccs_org_field`). Each column may hold only the
values on its list, and each value has one set of words that goes with
it.

The build stops before anything is published in two cases: a column
holds a value that is not on its list, or a value and its words
disagree.

```{r}
#| results: asis

derived_org_columns <- report$derived_org_columns

problems <- derived_org_columns$problems

has_problems <- nrow(problems) > 0

if (has_problems) {
  problems_table <- knitr::kable(
    problems,
    format = "html",
    col.names = c("Column", "Value", "Value in words", "Organizations", "Problem"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

  cat("**Failed.** The build found these problems:\n\n")

  print(problems_table)
}

if (!has_problems) {
  cat("**Passed.** Every value is on its list and matches its words.")
}
```

## Counts for each column

Each table gives the number of organizations for every value, the number
of blanks, and the change from the previous build. A column is blank
when the IRS code it comes from is blank.

```{r}
#| results: asis

has_previous_counts <- isTRUE(derived_org_columns$has_previous_counts)

if (!has_previous_counts) {
  cat("The previous build has no counts for these columns, so the tables show no change.")
}
```

```{r}
#| results: asis

# Show an unknown previous count or change as an empty cell, not as "NA".
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

#' Print the table of counts for one of the three columns
#'
#' @details
#' Writes a heading with the column's name, then one row per value. The
#' row for organizations with a blank is labelled "(blank)".
#'
#' @param value_column name of the column, for example "nccs_org_role".
#' @param counts the counts for all three columns, from the report.
#'
#' @return `value_column`, invisibly.
print_counts_for_one_value_column <- function(value_column, counts) {
  counts_for_column <- counts |>
    dplyr::filter(column == value_column) |>
    dplyr::mutate(value = dplyr::coalesce(value, "(blank)")) |>
    dplyr::select(value, definition, organizations, previous_organizations, change)

  counts_table <- knitr::kable(
    counts_for_column,
    format = "html",
    col.names = c("Value", "Value in words", "Organizations", "Previous build", "Change"),
    format.args = list(big.mark = ",")
  )

  cat(sprintf("\n\n### `%s`\n\n", value_column))

  print(counts_table)

  return(invisible(value_column))
}

value_columns <- unique(derived_org_columns$counts$column)

purrr::walk(
  value_columns,
  print_counts_for_one_value_column,
  counts = derived_org_columns$counts
)
```

# Notes

- **All output columns are VARCHAR.** The master build forces every
  column to string type so DuckDB's `UNION ALL BY NAME` can combine
  the legacy slim per-vintage schema with the current full schema
  without per-column type-mismatch errors. Cast in your downstream
  tool: `as.numeric(asset_amount)` in R,
  `pd.to_numeric(df['asset_amount'], errors='coerce')` in pandas, etc.
  Lat/lon in the geocoded master output are explicitly cast to
  DOUBLE.
- **Legacy-only EINs have sparse columns.** EINs whose latest
  appearance is in a pre-2014 legacy vintage carry only the legacy
  slim schema; current-pipeline-only columns (e.g. NTEEv2 fields,
  modern address quality flags) are NULL. The `bmf_source` column
  flags the source of each surviving row.
